overview: Early-modern Sweden supported both industrial communities and elaborate court art. Falun's copper landscape and Drottningholm's theatre reveal very different kinds of skilled work.

items.text: In the seventeenth century, Falun copper production helped make Sweden a major European metal producer. Mining shaped the surrounding economy and settlement landscape.
Falun's seventeenth-century planned town and mining settlements preserve evidence of workers' housing as well as production facilities. Industrial history includes the communities around the mine.
Drottningholm's eighteenth-century theatre used machinery that could change scenery while the curtain stayed up. Stage sets and working mechanisms survive.
Drottningholm's Chinese Pavilion reflects eighteenth-century European engagement with Asian design. Nearby Canton Village included manufacturing buildings and court living quarters.

sources.title: UNESCO, Mining Area of the Great Copper Mountain in Falun
